results.title: GitHub - fay-i/mermaid-mcp: Model Context Protocol server for rendering Mermaid diagrams to SVG, PDF, and deck artifacts. · GitHub
excerpts:
Mermaid MCP Server

Mermaid MCP Server is a TypeScript Model Context Protocol server for rendering Mermaid diagrams from MCP clients and AI coding workflows. It turns Mermaid source into SVG, PDF, and multi-page deck artifacts using Puppeteer, Mermaid CLI, and pdf-lib, with configurable themes, fonts, storage, and download URLs.
Use it when Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another MCP-capable workflow needs diagrams that are rendered as durable files instead of pasted source blocks. The server is intentionally focused: accept Mermaid code, render it consistently, and return an artifact reference your client can open, share, or attach to documentation.
High-Level Architecture

Features

* MCP server for Mermaid rendering : Exposes diagram tools over the Model Context Protocol
* High-quality rendering : Puppeteer + Mermaid CLI with Google Fonts and drop shadow support
* Multiple output formats : SVG and PDF with configurable themes ( default , dark , forest , neutral )
* Deck artifacts : Combine multiple diagrams into multi-page PDF presentations
* Flexible storage : Local filesystem or S3/MinIO with automatic backend detection
* Docker ready : Volume mount support for persistent artifact storage
* No telemetry : Runs as your local/server-side MCP process and does not add hidden tracking

Quick Start

Install from npm

# Install globally
npm install -g @fay-i/mermaid-mcp

# Run the MCP server with a data directory
mermaid-mcp ./data/artifacts

# Show help
mermaid-mcp --help
The server requires a data directory argument where generated SVG and PDF files will be stored. The directory will be created if it doesn't exist.

Use from an MCP client

Configure your MCP client to launch the mermaid-mcp binary and pass an artifact directory:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermaid-mcp": {
      "command": "mermaid-mcp",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/mermaid-artifacts"]
    }
  }
}
Or run the published package without a global install:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermaid-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@fay-i/mermaid-mcp", "/absolute/path/to/mermaid-artifacts"]
    }
  }
}

Connect to the deployed server

The deployed server speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP at one address:
* Transport | Address
* http | 10.42.1.81:8100/mcp
Any number of clients can connect at the same time. Each connection gets its own session, and the artifacts it renders are grouped under that session.
Add it to Claude Code:
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http mermaid-mcp 10.42.1.81:8100/mcp
If this machine added the server before, under the old SSE transport, remove that entry first, then run the add command above:
claude mcp remove --scope user mermaid-mcp
Clients still using the old SSE configuration get 410 Gone , with a message naming the address above.
To run your own HTTP server, pass --http=<port> . The server then serves /mcp on that port, plus /health for probes:
mermaid-mcp --http=8000 ./data/artifacts

...

export STORAGE_TYPE=s3

export MERMAID_S3_BUCKET=mermaid
export MERMAID_S3_ACCESS_KEY=minioadmin
export MERMAID_S3_SECRET_KEY=minioadmin

MCP Tools

excerpts:
Mermaid MCP Server

The Mermaid MCP Server enables AI assistants to create, validate, and render Mermaid diagrams seamlessly, plus full integration with your Mermaid account for advanced diagram management. When you ask your AI assistant to create a flowchart, sequence diagram, or any other Mermaid diagram, this server handles the entire process automatically - from syntax validation to PNG generation, interactive playground links, and direct integration with your Mermaid projects.

...

* SSE (Server-Sent Events) : mcp.mermaid.ai/sse with "type": "sse"
Authentication: Every tool call requires a valid Mermaid login — free to create — either through automatic OAuth or a manually configured Authorization header.

Available Tools

All tools listed below require Mermaid authentication (OAuth login or a manual token). Authentication is free: a Basic Mermaid account works, no paid plan required.

...

Authentication Setup

Every tool call requires you to be logged in to your Mermaid account. Signing up is free — the Basic tier costs nothing. There are two ways to authenticate:

Option 1: OAuth Login (recommended)

If your MCP client supports OAuth discovery, no manual token setup is required. The first time you call a tool, a browser window opens asking you to log in to your Mermaid account. Once you log in, your client stays authenticated automatically — no token needs to be added to your config.
Just use the plain, header-free configuration examples above.

Option 2: Manual Token-Based Authentication (still supported)

1. Get Your Token : Visit your Mermaid account settings and generate an API token
2. Add to Configuration : Include the token in the Authorization header as shown in the examples above
3. Replace Placeholder : Change YOUR_MERMAID_TOKEN_HERE with your actual token
If the token is missing or invalid, and OAuth login hasn’t completed, every tool call is rejected.

README.md

Mermaid MCP Server

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for validating Mermaid diagrams.
Implements a minimal Python wrapper over github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli for simpler out of the box use.

Overview

Python MCP server for validating Mermaid diagrams and (optionally) rendering them as PNG images. It uses the Mermaid CLI tool to perform the validation and rendering.
The server provides LLMs with structured validation results including:
* Boolean validation status ( is_valid: true/false ) indicating whether the Mermaid diagram syntax is correct
* Detailed error messages explaining exactly what went wrong if validation fails (e.g., syntax errors, unsupported diagram types, malformed nodes)
* Optional base64-encoded PNG images of successfully rendered diagrams for visual verification
This enables LLMs to programmatically validate Mermaid diagram syntax, understand specific errors to provide helpful corrections, and optionally receive visual confirmation of the rendered output.
Also provides a simple Pydantic-AI MCP Client to invoke the MCP server using a Gemini model for testing.

Prerequisites

Important : This MCP server requires Node.js to be installed on your system, even if you're only using the server component (not the client). The server internally calls npx @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli as a subprocess to perform diagram validation and rendering.

Required Dependencies

* Node.js with npm (required for all usage)
* Mermaid CLI : Install with npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
* Python with uv (for running the MCP server)

Quick Dependency Setup

# Install Mermaid CLI globally
npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli

# Verify installation
npx @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli --version

Quickstart

To use this server with an MCP client (like Claude Desktop), add the following configuration to your MCP settings:
Note : Make sure you have Node.js and Mermaid CLI installed (see Prerequisites above) before configuring the MCP server.

Configuration Format

1. Clone this repository
2. Add this to your MCP client configuration file (e.g., claude_desktop_config.json ):
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermaid-validator": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "/path/to/mermaid_mcp_server.py"],
    }
  }
}

Configuration Options

* command : Use uv to run the server
* args : Run the server script with uv run
* cwd : Set to the absolute path of your cloned repository
* env : Environment variables for the server
* MCP_TRANSPORT : Set to "stdio" for standard input/output communication

Example Extended Configuration

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermaid-validator": {
      "command": "uv", 
      "args": ["run", "/path/to/mermaid_mcp_server.py"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_TRANSPORT": "stdio",
      }
    }
  }
}

Abstractions Over Mermaid-CLI

The Python wrapper significantly simplifies the usage of the Mermaid CLI by abstracting away complex file handling and command-line arguments:

Without the wrapper (raw mermaid-cli):

...

4. Error Handling : Captures and returns structured error messages instead of raw stderr output
5. Command Construction : Builds the complete npx @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli command with all necessary flags
6. Resource Cleanup : Ensures all temporary files are properly deleted after processing
This abstraction allows users to focus on diagram validation and rendering without dealing with the underlying file system operations and command-line complexities.

Local Development

This repository can be used standalone to test the functionality of the Mermaid MCP validator programmatically.

Requirements

See the Prerequisites section above for required dependencies (Node.js, Mermaid CLI, and Python with uv).

Quick Setup (Recommended)

Use the provided Makefile for streamlined setup:
# Install all dependencies (Python + Node.js + Mermaid CLI)
make install

# Run validation tests
make test

Manual Setup

If you prefer manual setup:
1. Clone this repository
2. Install dependencies: uv sync
3. Install Mermaid CLI: npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
4. Copy .env.example to .env and fill in your API key
5. Run the server: uv run mermaid_mcp_server.py

Usage

The server exposes a tool for validating Mermaid diagrams:
* validate_mermaid_diagram : Validates a Mermaid diagram and returns validation results

Tool Parameters

* diagram_text (required): The Mermaid diagram text to validate
* return_image (optional, default: false ): Whether to return the base64-encoded PNG image

Context Length Optimisation

Important : By default, the tool does not return the base64-encoded image ( return_image=false ) to preserve context length in LLM conversations. Base64-encoded images can be very long strings (often 10KB-100KB+) that significantly impact the available context for the conversation.
When to use each setting :
* return_image=false (default): Use for diagram validation only. Fast and context-efficient.
* return_image=true : Use only when you specifically need the rendered image data. Warning: This will consume significant context length.

Example Usage

# Validation only (recommended for most cases)
result = await validate_mermaid_diagram("graph TD; A-->B")
# Returns: MermaidValidationResult(is_valid=True, error_message=None, diagram_image=None)

# Validation with image (use sparingly)
result = await validate_mermaid_diagram("graph TD; A-->B", return_image=True)
# Returns: MermaidValidationResult(is_valid=True, error_message=None, diagram_image="iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg...")

Testing

The project includes convenient testing commands:
# Run all tests
make test

# Or run the test script directly
uv run test_pydantic.py
The test script uses Pydantic AI with Gemini models to validate the MCP server functionality.

results.title: Mermaid API skill — Mermaid Chart
excerpts:
Mermaid API skill

Ask your coding agent to check or draw a Mermaid diagram, and it does it for you through Mermaid API. With the mermaid-api skill installed, your agent can:
* Validate diagram code. When the code is invalid, the API reports the line and column where the parser stopped, and the agent fixes the code there and checks again.
* Render a diagram to an SVG, PNG or PDF file at the path you name.

...

You need:
* A coding agent that can run shell commands and supports Agent Skills : Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.
* macOS, Linux or WSL. Native Windows PowerShell is not supported.
* curl , and ideally jq . jq ships with macOS 15 and later and most Linux distributions; without it the agent still works, using temporary files.
* A Mermaid API key. Some calls cost API credits; see What it costs . Use a personal key for stored diagrams.

Install the skill

In Claude Code , use the plugin marketplace:
/plugin marketplace add Mermaid-Chart/skills /plugin install mermaid-api@mermaid
In any other agent , use the skills CLI :
npx  skills  add  Mermaid-Chart/skills
Install by hand instead
Copy the skills/mermaid-api folder from the Mermaid-Chart/skills repository into your agent’s skills folder:
* Agent | All projects | One project
* Claude Code | ~/.claude/skills/ | .claude/skills/
* Codex, Cursor and agents reading .agents/ | ~/.agents/skills/ | .agents/skills/

Set up your API key

The first time you ask for a diagram without a key, the agent walks you through this. You can also do it up front.
1. Open the Mermaid API console and create a key. It is shown once , so copy it.
2. In your own terminal , not through the agent, run this and paste the key when asked. Nothing is shown as you paste.
mkdir  -p  ~/.config/mermaid-api  && ( umask  077 ;  printf  'Mermaid API key: ' ;  read  -rs  k  &&  printf  'Authorization: Bearer %s\n'  " $k "  >  ~/.config/mermaid-api/credentials ;  echo )
3. Tell the agent you’re done. It checks the key, for free, and tells you how many credits you have.
The key is saved in ~/.config/mermaid-api/credentials . See Reference if you’d rather create that file yourself or use an environment variable.

...

What the agent runs
Every command starts with two lines that pick the API URL and pass your key to curl without showing it:
api = ${MERMAID_API_URL :- https :// api.mermaid.ai} if  [  -n  " $MERMAID_API_KEY "  ];  then  auth = ( -H  "Authorization: Bearer  $MERMAID_API_KEY " );  else  auth = ( -H  @" $HOME /.config/mermaid-api/credentials" );  fi
Validate reads the file in place:
jq  -Rs  '{code: .}'  checkout.mmd  |  curl  -sS  " $api /v1/validate"  "${ auth [ @ ]}"  -H  'Content-Type: application/json'  --data  @-
Render writes to a temporary file and moves it into place only on success:
tmp = $( mktemp ) status = $( jq  -Rs  '{code: ., format: "png"}'  checkout.mmd  |  curl  -sS  -o  " $tmp "  -w  '%{http_code}'  " $api /v1/render"  "${ auth [ @ ]}"  -H  'Content-Type: application/json'  --data  @- ) if  [  " $status "  =  200  ];  then  mv  " $tmp "  docs/checkout.png  &&  chmod  644  docs/checkout.png ;  else  cat  " $tmp " ;  rm  -f  " $tmp " ;  fi

Open API Client
Powered by Scalar

Mermaid API

Download OpenAPI Document
json Download OpenAPI Document
yaml
Mermaid API validates and renders Mermaid diagrams for programs: agents, LLM tool calls, CI pipelines and products. Validate says whether diagram code is valid and why not; render turns it into SVG, PNG or PDF, with the latest Mermaid unless the call pins an earlier one; generate asks Mermaid AI for diagram code from a prompt, and repair asks it to fix invalid code. The operations below are the contract; this guide is what they do not say by themselves.

...

Beta

Mermaid API is in beta. Request and response fields may be added, renamed or removed; defaults, limits and ceilings may move; the latest Mermaid version bumps without notice, so the same code may render differently over time unless the call pins a version. What does not change: the /v1 prefix, the error structure, every error code once shipped, and bearer authentication. An endpoint whose request or response takes a new shape gets a /v2 path beside its /v1 one, which keeps working unchanged; other breaking changes are announced, not versioned: each is listed in the changelog at the end of this guide with its date and what a caller must do. Every response carries x-mermaid-api-phase: beta until general availability. Do not build a production dependency on it yet.

Authentication

Every /v1 call except the reference endpoints needs an API key: Authorization: Bearer <key> . Keys are created in the console by any Mermaid Chart user, shown once at creation, and have no expiry by default. A key is <prefix>.<secret> , the prefix mmd_ and twelve hex digits; the prefix appears in listings, the secret is stored only as a hash. A refused key is 401 with www-authenticate: Bearer and one of ERR_KEY_MISSING , ERR_KEY_UNKNOWN , ERR_KEY_REVOKED , ERR_KEY_EXPIRED : fix the key, do not retry. ERR_KEY_OWNER_DELETED means Mermaid Chart no longer knows the key's owner: the key works again once it does, within 5 minutes. The examples below take the key from $MERMAID_API_KEY .

Validate

POST /v1/validate , a valid diagram:
curl -s  "api.mermaid.ai/v1/validate"  \
  -H  "Authorization: Bearer  $MERMAID_API_KEY "  \
  -H  "Content-Type: application/json"  \
  -d  '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]"}'
{ "valid" : true , "diagramType" : "flowchart-v2" }

# mermaid-cli

This is a command-line interface (CLI) for mermaid. It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output. There's basic support for converting mermaid code blocks embedded within Markdown files.

```
npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
```

mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.svg

Mermaid MCP Server

Mermaid MCP Server is a TypeScript Model Context Protocol server for rendering Mermaid diagrams from MCP clients and AI coding workflows. It turns Mermaid source into SVG, PDF, and multi-page deck artifacts using Puppeteer, Mermaid CLI, and pdf-lib, with configurable themes, fonts, storage, and download URLs.
Use it when Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another MCP-capable workflow needs diagrams that are rendered as durable files instead of pasted source blocks. The server is intentionally focused: accept Mermaid code, render it consistently, and return an artifact reference your client can open, share, or attach to documentation.
High-Level Architecture

Features

* MCP server for Mermaid rendering : Exposes diagram tools over the Model Context Protocol
* High-quality rendering : Puppeteer + Mermaid CLI with Google Fonts and drop shadow support
* Multiple output formats : SVG and PDF with configurable themes ( default , dark , forest , neutral )
* Deck artifacts : Combine multiple diagrams into multi-page PDF presentations
* Flexible storage : Local filesystem or S3/MinIO with automatic backend detection
* Docker ready : Volume mount support for persistent artifact storage
* No telemetry : Runs as your local/server-side MCP process and does not add hidden tracking

Quick Start

Install from npm

# Install globally
npm install -g @fay-i/mermaid-mcp

# Run the MCP server with a data directory
mermaid-mcp ./data/artifacts

# Show help
mermaid-mcp --help
The server requires a data directory argument where generated SVG and PDF files will be stored. The directory will be created if it doesn't exist.

Use from an MCP client

Configure your MCP client to launch the mermaid-mcp binary and pass an artifact directory:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mermaid-mcp": {

README.md

Mermaid MCP Server

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for validating Mermaid diagrams.
Implements a minimal Python wrapper over github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli for simpler out of the box use.

Overview

Python MCP server for validating Mermaid diagrams and (optionally) rendering them as PNG images. It uses the Mermaid CLI tool to perform the validation and rendering.
The server provides LLMs with structured validation results including:
* Boolean validation status ( is_valid: true/false ) indicating whether the Mermaid diagram syntax is correct
* Detailed error messages explaining exactly what went wrong if validation fails (e.g., syntax errors, unsupported diagram types, malformed nodes)
* Optional base64-encoded PNG images of successfully rendered diagrams for visual verification
This enables LLMs to programmatically validate Mermaid diagram syntax, understand specific errors to provide helpful corrections, and optionally receive visual confirmation of the rendered output.
Also provides a simple Pydantic-AI MCP Client to invoke the MCP server using a Gemini model for testing.
